report:
Reviewed the complete identity-only claim, all four ordinary implementation associations, and the sole explicit TODO test. Additional module-expansion and enum-identity helpers used in this assessment are captured through review read. No production or test sources were edited.

The claim forbids hidden receiver inference, associated-type normalization, trait-obligation proof, and applicable-method selection during ordinary name/path lookup. Resolver::resolve_path, resolve_name_from_scope, and their module/import helpers return existing Resolution or Symbol identities. Rib lookup returns a copied Local/Param/Sym/SelfTy entry from the lexical environment; returning an already supplied SelfTy is not inference or normalization. Multi-segment paths follow named module/enum identities, while the FIXME for T::Item explicitly does not invoke a solver. Module lookup follows imports, scopes, namespaces, external metadata and preludes; it does not enter function signatures, inference contexts, obligation solving, or applicable-method selection. traits_in_method_scope enumerates trait identities plus completeness flags; signature accessor methods in symbol/mod.rs are separate consumers, not calls from provider enumeration.

The symbol/mod.rs children association returns module members or enum variants, and named_children filters external exported metadata by name and namespace before constructing identities. Captured enum_variants builds LocalVariantSym/constructor identities from parsed variant syntax and spans without calling enum sig; its separate signature lowering is not used by children. Captured local module membership performs declaration macro expansion and syntax parsing to discover identities, with completeness checks for unresolved expansions. Such expansion is needed to know the declaration set and is not checked-body evaluation or method applicability. The newly introduced generated-root import audit likewise compares binding origins and resolved definition identities only. It retains the existing combined lookup during expansion and does not add inference or solver calls to resolution.

The associated semantic_spec::todo::resolution_lookup_identity_only explicitly defers a normalized query trace demonstrating scope/import/metadata-only execution and excluding inference, trait solver, candidate-signature, and checked-body execution. That is adequate, visible accounting for missing verification, not a behavioral test. Completing the anchor requires trace-based assertions on representative local, imported, external and generated paths, including cache states; source inspection and unrelated passing compile fixtures are insufficient to establish the absence of hidden queries. There are no N/A entries. The ordinary implementation associations establish the inspected architectural boundary, while test status remains TODO. This review ran start/read/record commands only and claims no new behavioral test execution. No new violation or required edit was found in the changed identity lookup code.
